previous_assumption: Once `PermissionService` grew the organization-type check (Rental's Step 1: authorization model correction), `EquipmentService.requireRentalCompanyOrganization` and its `OrganizationRepositoryPort` constructor dependency could be deleted as a clean, self-contained follow-up with nothing else to touch.
correction: Deleting the method left a dangling orphaned JSDoc comment block (no method under it) and an unused `organizationRepository` constructor parameter that no longer compiled (`Cannot find name 'OrganizationRepositoryPort'` — its import had been removed but the parameter using it hadn't). Also required: dropping the now-extra `organizationRepository` argument from `EquipmentService`'s instantiation in `container.ts`, and reworking both `apps/api/test/permission-service.test.ts` (added a parameterized `fakeOrganizationRepository(organizationTypeCode)` plus a new test proving the org-type gate denies a permission the role would otherwise grant) and `apps/api/test/equipment-service.test.ts` (`fakePermissionService` now takes an `organizationTypeCode` param instead of `EquipmentService` taking an `OrganizationRepositoryPort` directly; the Renter-rejection test now varies the `PermissionService` passed in, not a repository passed to `EquipmentService`). Verified end-to-end with a live signup+curl check (Renter 403, Rental Company 201/200) against the shared layer, not the old per-service patch. Lesson: a "delete the stopgap" step in a refactor is never purely subtractive — grep for every constructor call site (including test fakes) before assuming a dependency removal is self-contained.
